title: Dangerous Goods Acceptance: How Long an Approval Covers Loading
content:
## Clause

An approval under Dangerous Goods Acceptance does not cover loading indefinitely. It covers loading up to and including the last day of the category's approval period, which is found by moving forward from the approval date recorded on the acceptance by the number of calendar days in that period. Loading that takes place on that last day is still covered. Goods that have not been loaded when the period has run out go back to review, as an approval reopened under the product's amendment and re-review rules.

## Elements of the time limit

| Element | Content |
|---|---|
| Event that starts the clock | the approval of the acceptance |
| Record relied on | the approval date on the acceptance record |
| Length | the category's approval period, in calendar days |
| Counting | calendar dates, starting from the approval date |
| Comparison | loading date not later than the last day |
| Last day itself | covered |
| When not met | the goods return to review |

## Hypothetical boundary cases

The period below is invented for illustration. With an approval dated 2026-06-03 and a 12-day period, the last covered day is 2026-06-15.

- Loading on 2026-06-15: covered by the approval.
- Loading on 2026-06-14: covered.
- Goods still unloaded after 2026-06-15: the approval no longer covers them and the file returns to review.

## Point of judgement

**Does the hour at which the approval was given matter?** It does not. The period runs on calendar dates from the approval date, so only the date counts.
